record.paper_title: Open Problems Related to Quantum Query Complexity
record.original_question: Does there exist an oracle relative to which BQP differs from IP_BQP, where IP_BQP is the subclass of BQP consisting of languages whose yes instances can be proved by a BQP prover to a BPP verifier through polynomially many rounds of classical interaction?

evidence.quote: Now let IPBQP be the subclass of BQP consisting of all languages for which a BQP prover can convince a BPP verifier of a “yes” answer, through polynomially many rounds of classical interaction.
Problem 8 Is there at least an oracle relative to which BQP̸= IPBQP?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Background and definitions:

- BPP is the class of languages decided by polynomial-time probabilistic Turing machines with two-sided bounded error.
- BQP is the class of languages decided by polynomial-time quantum Turing machines with two-sided bounded error.
- For an oracle O, BPP^O and BQP^O denote the corresponding classes when both verifier and prover have access to the oracle O.
- Define IP_BQP to be the subclass of BQP consisting of all languages L such that there exists a polynomial-round interactive protocol with purely classical communication between a BQP prover P and a BPP verifier V satisfying:
  (Completeness) For every x ∈ L, V interacting with P accepts with probability at least 2/3.
  (Soundness) For every x ∉ L and every (computationally unbounded) prover P*, V interacting with P* accepts with probability at most 1/3.
  Here the number of rounds is bounded by a polynomial in |x|, and all messages exchanged are classical bit strings of polynomial length.
- The relativized class IP_BQP^O is defined analogously, with both the verifier and the prover having oracle access to O.

Question: Does there exist an oracle O such that BQP^O ≠ IP_BQP^O? Equivalently, exhibit (or prove the existence of) an oracle O and a language L ∈ BQP^O for which no BQP^O prover can convince a BPP^O verifier of membership in L through any polynomial-round classical interactive protocol satisfying the above completeness and soundness conditions.
artifact.category_tag: quantum query complexity and oracle separations
artifact.status_search_result: The problem of finding an oracle separating BQP from IP_BQP (whether a BQP prover can convince a BPP verifier, via classical interaction, of every language in BQP) is listed among current open problems in quantum query complexity. Web search did not surface any resolution; related oracle-separation results (e.g., Raz–Tal for BQP vs PH) do not address this question. The status appears to remain open.

status_evidence.title: Open Problems Related to Quantum Query Complexity
status_evidence.snippet: Quantum query complexity still has enticing open problems ranging from relativized QMA versus QCMA and BQP versus IP, to time/space tradeoffs.
status_evidence.claim: Listed as an open problem regarding BQP versus an interactive variant.

status_evidence.title: Oracle Separation of BQP and PH (Raz–Tal)
status_evidence.snippet: Raz and Tal give an oracle relative to which BQP is not contained in PH.
status_evidence.claim: A different oracle separation result; does not resolve BQP vs IP_BQP.
